name: Emera Inc.
moat_justification: Regulated franchise monopolies — Tampa Electric and Peoples Gas in Florida, Nova Scotia Power, Barbados Light & Power and other regulated electric/gas utilities — give durable, regulator-granted exclusivity and a visible rate-base growth runway ($20B 2026-2030 capital plan, 7-8% rate-base CAGR guided, ~80% directed to Florida), but earned returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs and the measured franchise earns little above its cost of capital: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json runs 2.8% / 4.5% / 5.0% / 2.6% / 5.3% for FY2021-FY2025 (after-tax operating income over equity + debt - cash, CAD as filed; gross margin is not meaningful for this filer — fundamentals.json carries no COGS split, gross_margin null). That is a moderate/narrow moat: durable cash flows, capped economics.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 4.1%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CAD converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Emera Inc. Form 40-F / FY2025 reporting: the Corporation's common shares are listed directly on the TSX and NYSE under the symbol EMA (every earnings release header reads TSX/NYSE: EMA); there is no depositary or ADS program — the NYSE line is the same common shares. The FY2025 statements' EPS note (Note 13) denominator — weighted average diluted shares 299.7M — matches the engine's shares_diluted_latest exactly, confirming filed per-share figures and the NYSE price are on the same share basis.) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low

one_liner: High-quality regulated utility, moat 5/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in every filed year (rate-base growth capex runs well ahead of operating cash flow) — no positive normalized OE, so it cannot clear any hurdle on this model; Tier F by construction, confidence low (utility sector-model mismatch).
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Regulated franchise monopolies — exclusive electric and gas service territories in Florida (Tampa Electric, Peoples Gas), Nova Scotia, New Mexico, Barbados and Grand Bahama; ~2.6 million customers
Visible rate-base growth: $20B 2026-2030 capital plan driving guided 7-8% rate-base CAGR and 5-7% adjusted EPS growth through 2030, ~80% of the plan directed to Florida
Florida weight: Florida operations contribute roughly 70% of adjusted earnings, riding population and customer growth in one of the fastest-growing U.S. utility territories
Essential-service, low-cyclicality demand; Q2 2026 year-to-date operating cash flow up 8% year over year even in a softer EPS quarter
Regulatory clarity into 2028 at Peoples Gas (2025 rate case complete) and a consensus settlement path at Nova Scotia Power filed September 2025
moat_against: Returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs — no pricing power; measured ROIC proxy has run only ~2.6-5.3% over the last five fiscal years
Nova Scotia political/regulatory risk: provincial rate-cap politics around Nova Scotia Power and fuel-cost recovery have repeatedly overridden normal rate-making

Heavy leverage (net debt $15.67B per dcf_numbers.json) plus a $20B funding plan — rate-sensitive financing costs and perpetual equity issuance (share count +4.1%/yr per the engine blend: DRIP and ATM issuance)
Storm and climate exposure concentrated in Florida and the Caribbean (hurricane hardening is a large, ongoing share of capex)

Pending all-share merger with Canadian Utilities (announced October 6, 2026; ~$72B combined enterprise value, close targeted Q3-Q4 2027) — approval, integration and leverage risk sits on top of the standalone plan; CAD/USD translation exposure on U.S.-dollar earnings
